Hi Brandon

You've posted in the Thunderbird Android forum. The community over on the desktop forum are much better placed to help you with the TB desktop portion of your question.

Thunderbird Android

Thunderbird Android does not offer any extension capability, API or MCP URL. The application data is stored in it's own app sandbox within Androids secure data partition. This is inaccessible on non rooted phones. I therefore don't think there is a realistic way for an LLM to have access.

Feel free to raise a feature request on Mozilla connect. The community can then vote and comment on your idea.

Thunderbird Desktop

I don't have experience with Thunderbird desktop or LLM integrations. I've done a quick web search which suggests there may be some options available to you via Third Party applications and extensions.

The below github project seems very close to what your looking for. https://github.com/agimenezdev/thunderbird-mcp

A read-only MCP server that lets an LLM search and read your Thunderbird email — locally, with no IMAP connection and no credentials. It works by querying Thunderbird's own full-text index (GLODA, the global-messages-db.sqlite that Thunderbird already maintains). The server takes an atomic snapshot of that database and exposes a handful of focused tools to any MCP client: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or the Agent SDK.

The below AI-Mail Thunderbird Add-on might also offer an avenue for you. https://addons.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/addon/ai-mail-support/

New models: Anthropic Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash, OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, SpaceXAI Grok 4.7

Again, try posting within the desktop forum as it's possible the community there may have some experience on the topic.

I should first caveat that it's not possible to verify an emails legitimacy from a screen shot.

Have you just setup Thunderbird for Android on a Galaxy A33 phone today?

If you did, receiving a genuine message originating from gmail would be reasonable. The app normally requests you to login and grant it access to your account during account setup.

If this was not completed by you and therefore unexpected, I'd recommend investigating further.
